evidence_concerns.message: Table D2's construct-design rate for Gemini 4 Argon at low effort, 31.9%, cannot be a mean of binary outcomes over the stated 15 tasks times 5 attempts: no integer numerator over 75 falls in its rounding window [23.8875, 23.9625], while all 23 other printed construct rates do. Its printed 95% interval [10.7, 52.0] is also byte-identical to the same system's top-effort interval. The two signals together indicate a transcription fault in the paper rather than a measured value, and the paper prints nothing that resolves it: the lane's aggregate is 15.8 under either 31.9 or 32.0, and Table G2's per-task solves are top-effort only. The printed value is kept as published and this entry withholds it from automatic comparison; the lane's other results are not covered.
evidence_concerns.source_locator: Table D2, row 'Gemini 4 Argon' tier 'low' effort 'low', column 'Construct design % [95% CI]'

limitations: Preprint, not peer reviewed. The benchmark is published by Benchling with DNAForge, and the authors both built the benchmark and ran every system on it.

Scores come from a cloning simulator and retrospective graders, not from constructs built at the bench; the authors state the simulator cannot capture every source of variation in reagents, handling, growth or reaction outcomes (Section 6.2).

Ten of the fifteen construct-design tasks are graded in part by GPT-6 Astra as a rubric judge, which is also one of the eight evaluated systems; the authors record occasional grading inconsistency as a limitation (Section 6.2).
The simulator reports only the first blocking error, so the failure categories in Tables E1 and E2 do not establish whether later steps would have succeeded (Section 6.2).
Single-turn: the authors state the format does not reflect the multi-turn way scientists work with a model (Section 6.2).

The construct-design tasks, graders and reference solutions are said in footnote 1 (page 3) to be available at https://github.com/benchling/benchbench-cloning. That URL returned HTTP 404 from both the web page and the GitHub API on 2026-11-06 at 2026-11-06T11:51:23Z, a repository search for 'benchbench-cloning' returned no results, and the repository is absent from benchling's public repositories. No code or data artifact was retrieved.

description: Technical report for HyCell, with its architecture and training, a benchmark of frozen embeddings of eleven models on seven held-out atlases, downstream analyses and fine-tuning.

attributes.extraction_method: pdftotext -layout text layer, parsed by extract/parse.py with every row label and cell count asserted.
limitations: Author-released report, not peer reviewed. The developer of HyCell ran every model, so no result is independent of the developer.
No uncertainty is printed anywhere in the report: no interval, standard deviation or test for any score, including the 0.735 against 0.736 comparison with Stack.

The comparators do not run under equal conditions. Stack encodes sets of 256 cells with the cells of each batch together, so it uses batch labels at inference; SCimilarity and scPRINT are trained with cell-type labels; PCA is fitted to each evaluation atlas on 2,000 highly variable genes. HyCell embeds each cell from its own counts with no batch or donor information.

The benchmark measures cell-level tasks only. Stack draws on the other cells of a sample at inference, which the report says helps sample-level tasks such as predicting a donor's disease state; such tasks are not in the benchmark.

The composite S = 0.3 Bio + 0.2 Batch + 0.25 LR + 0.25 kNN is the authors' chosen weighting. Table 4 prints only S per atlas, not its four components per atlas, so the per-atlas weighting cannot be checked.

The seven atlases are stated to be excluded from HyCell's pretraining corpus. The report does not say whether the ten published comparators were pretrained on cells of these atlases, and several are trained on CELLxGENE data, so the comparison is not shown to be held out for them.

name: HyInv Technical Report (Hyra Team, 2026-10-14)
description: Technical report for HyInv, with the five-panel inverse-folding comparison against ten published baselines, the sampler and numerics ablations, the inference-time measurements and the four application protocols.

attributes.archive_note: The PDF itself is not committed; its gzipped text layer is in artifacts/HyInv_Technical_Report.txt.gz and the PDF can be refetched at the pinned commit and checked against artifact_sha256.
attributes.archive_transformation_receipt: gzip -n9 of the pdftotext -layout output of the pinned PDF (poppler pdftotext, macOS).

evidence_concerns.message: Appendix C states 'We do not claim zero sequence overlap between the training data and the evaluation panels', and Appendix G's homology screen is a coverage rule under which partial hits remain (Table 10: 28 of 74 de novo backbones and 7 of 12 pocket backbones have partial hits, and all 4 named enzymes are homologous to training data by design). Results on these panels are therefore not clean held-out measurements and must not be compared with results from sources that do establish no overlap.
evidence_concerns.source_locator: Appendix C 'Data and pool', final bullet; Appendix G 'Homology of the panels' and Table 10

evidence_concerns.message: The ten baselines are single published settings at one temperature each, so their design-set diversity differs from HyInv's: on CATH4.3 test HyInv samples at diversity 0.331 against 0.093 for PiFold, 0.104 for CMLM, 0.144 for LM-Design 650M and 0.000 for DPLM-2 3B, which decodes by argmax. Appendix D.2 states that these four differences are not at matched diversity, and Appendix A states that even for the closest baselines the comparisons are 'close to, but not exactly at, equal diversity', the largest offset of 0.016 being worth at most 0.0011 scTM at the development slope. The scTM and scTM difference results of the protocols named here must not be read as a matched-diversity ranking. The results read at a stated diversity level (Tables 8 and 9 and Appendix D.3) are not covered by this entry, because they are the ones the report reads on a fitted curve at a fixed diversity; nor are the recovery, diversity, pLDDT, scRMSD and lDDT results, whose protocols carry the same single-setting caveat in their own limitations and whose metric qualifiers say the value is at each method's own setting.
evidence_concerns.source_locator: Appendix D.1 and D.2; Table 7; Figure 14 diversity block; Section 5.1 'Baselines' and 'HyInv'

evidence_concerns.message: The inference-time results were measured with the supervised-stage weights and a rewrite temperature of 0.23, not with the released checkpoint and its default temperatures, and the quality read-outs of the two numerical paths used the RL checkpoint at update 288, not update 640. Speed and quality in this report are therefore measured on different weights, and the 57x figure compares HyInv's optimised BF16 path with ProteinMPNN's released implementation rather than with an equally optimised baseline.
evidence_concerns.source_locator: Table 1 footnote; Appendix F 'Timing protocol' and 'Baseline timings'

attributes.extraction_method: pdftotext -layout text layer, parsed by extract/parse.py with every row label and column count asserted.
limitations: Author-released report, not peer reviewed and not independently refereed. All three authors are at Tencent Hunyuan, which released the model, and the baselines were run by the same team.

Every quantity is computed on predicted structures and designed sequences. Appendix B states that none is an experimental measurement, so no binding, stability or activity is measured anywhere in the report.

Appendix C states: 'We do not claim zero sequence overlap between the training data and the evaluation panels.' The RL pool was filtered against the panels with a same-source homology mask and the supervised corpus by exact-sequence removal and a homology filter, which is weaker than no overlap.

The ten baselines are each at one published single-temperature setting and were not tuned to the panels, so the scTM comparisons are at comparable rather than equal sequence diversity. Appendix D.2 states that PiFold, CMLM, LM-Design and DPLM-2 3B are single points at much lower diversity than HyInv.

ESMFold2 is both the primary scoring predictor and the reinforcement-learning reward, so the five ESMFold2 panels favour the trained model by construction; only RecentPDB is also folded by Boltz2 and Protenix2.

Some baseline ESMFold2 cells were regenerated for the report rather than taken from the released scores (Table 5), and the ProteinMPNN temperatures other than the published one were generated for the report.

Appendix A records run-to-run noise of about +/-0.0015 scTM per panel and says differences between checkpoints below about 0.003 are not resolvable; intervals are not adjusted for multiple comparisons.

Latencies were measured on one NVIDIA H20 and exclude model loading, CUDA graph capture and kernel compilation. Baselines ran as released, unbatched where the released adapter handles one structure per call, so Appendix F states the speed-ups are against those implementations and not against the best achievable speed of the baseline models.

Figures 1, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9b, 11c, 13, 16 and 17 carry results that are not printed as labelled cells, or whose bar order cannot be recovered from the text layer; they are recorded as gaps in notes.md, not read by eye.
attributes.version_note: Page 1 of the report prints the date 2026-10-14, which is the date issue #232 records and the one kept in version. The pinned PDF's own metadata gives CreationDate and ModDate D:20261030105208+08'00' (2026-10-30 02:52 UTC), produced by pdfTeX-1.40.25, so the bytes that carry artifact_sha256 were typeset sixteen days after the printed date. No earlier PDF of this report is published at or before the pinned commit, so the two dates cannot be compared against another version of the bytes, and nothing in the batch rests on either date beyond naming the report.

evidence_concerns.message: Appendix A states that for GB1 two-vs-rest, GB1 three-vs-rest and the cross-protein hydrolase split of FLIP2, validation data come from the training distribution while the test sets are strongly shifted, so probe selection is dominated by noise and numerically equivalent runs of the same model differ by up to 0.2. The authors print these cells but leave them out of every summary statistic.

limitations: Author-released report, not peer reviewed. All three authors are at Tencent Hunyuan, which released the model, and every baseline was run by the same team through its own adapters; no result here is independent of the developer.

All accuracy results were computed with BF16 arithmetic. The released default is the INT8 engine, for which the report prints no per-task value; it states only that INT8 keeps zero-shot fitness, structure, function annotation and likelihood within 0.01 of the BF16 results.

Section 4 states that confidence intervals are paired bootstrap intervals, but the report prints intervals only for four ProteinGym paired differences. Every table cell is printed without its interval.

Tables 6 and 7 print every task for 13 of the 29 models only. The other 16 checkpoints appear at most in Figure 3a, Table 3, Table 5 or the prose, and 8 of the 28 public checkpoints are never named with a value, so the report's list of 28 cannot be reconstructed from it.
Table 5's rows without a dagger are published ProteinGym leaderboard values at commit 144fe22, quoted rather than run by the authors; they are not recorded from this source.

Throughput was measured on one NVIDIA H20 with the INT8 engine for HyPLM-Flash and with reference implementations for the baselines, each with the fastest attention kernel its implementation supports. Only HyPLM-Flash's own figure and the baselines' range are printed.

limitations: Preprint, not peer reviewed. No published version was found (bioRxiv publication API, 2026-10-13).
Results are printed only as aggregates: Table 2 over all 24 tasks and Table 4 per domain. Per-task leaderboard percentiles appear only as points in Figures 2 and 4, with no printed values.

Table 3 names two protein engineering tasks differently from the repository's task list at commit 673f3d8 (experiments/biomlbench_v0.1a.txt): SPA_STAAU_Tsuboyama_2023 (protein A) versus SBI_STAAM_Tsuboyama_2023_2JVG (immunoglobulin-binding protein Sbi, single substitutions), and PSAE_PICP2_indels versus PSAE_PICP2_Tsuboyama_2023_1PSE (the substitution assay; the repository also holds a separate _indels task). Which of these assays were run is unresolved. The third label difference, CBX4_HUMAN_multi-sub versus CBX4_HUMAN_Tsuboyama_2023_2K28, is the same assay: the repository description of 2K28 says it contains multi-substitution variants of CBX4_HUMAN.

Table 4 prints a value with a plus-or-minus spread but its caption does not say what the spread is. Figures 2 and 4 show the same per-domain leaderboard percentiles as mean ± SEM across tasks, and the Table 2 caption refers to the reported SEM.

Section 3.4 defines Above Median, Any Medal and Completion Rate over tasks, but the Table 4 values are multiples of 1/(4 x tasks in the domain) (for example 45.8% = 11/24 for 6 protein tasks), which fits counting replicate runs. The denominator is unresolved.
Table 4 prints Completion Rate 'NA' for Dummy in the penalized block, while Table 2 prints 100.0 for Dummy overall.
All agents were run by the benchmark's authors, who did not build them. B. T. is CTO of ScienceMachine, which provided compute and LLM API resources (Competing Interests; Acknowledgments).

Version 3 replaced the STELLA rows for Drug Discovery and Protein Engineering in Table 4 (and STELLA's Table 2 rows) with new values without explaining why in the text; for example STELLA's penalized protein engineering leaderboard percentile is 14.78 in v2 and 34.98 in v3, and its completion rate 87.5 and 100.0. The other agents' rows are unchanged, including their Mean Rank, which leaves the Mean Rank columns of those blocks internally inconsistent (they no longer sum to 15). Those 20 Mean Rank results are marked disputed.

Section 4.2 says Biomni leads Protein Engineering with penalties applied; that sentence is unchanged from v2. In v3 Table 4 STELLA has the higher penalized protein engineering leaderboard percentile (34.98 vs 29.93) and Above Median (45.8 vs 25.0); Biomni has the better Mean Rank (2.00 vs 2.33).
M. G. is a contract employee of ScienceMachine, as well as B. T. being its CTO (Competing Interests).

limitations: The repository holds no agent results or leaderboard snapshots; the human leaderboards are fetched from upstream services at grading time.

Agent configuration files are the repository defaults at this commit. The paper does not say the reported runs used exactly these files, and some differ from Section 3 (STELLA's model, per-agent time limits).

Time limits: the runner overrides each agent's TIME_LIMIT_SECS with the task's time_limit when one is set (biomlbench/agents.py, agents/registry.py). 18 of the 20 in-scope tasks set 28800 s (8 hours), matching Section 3.4. Q8EG35_SHEON_Campbell_2022_indels and CSN4_MOUSE_Tsuboyama_2023_1UFM_indels set none, so the agent default would apply (43200 s for AIDE, Biomni and MLAgentBench; 57600 s for STELLA).

Reference leaderboards are not all human submissions: for ProteinGym tasks the leaderboard is the row of ProteinGym's own leaderboard for that assay, one entry per published model (biomlbench/data_sources/proteingym.py, with a placeholder submission date), and the Open Problems spatially-variable-genes description says its leaderboard 'is comprised of existing methods'. The manual (Open Problems) data source returns an empty leaderboard at this commit, so how the single-cell leaderboards were built is not recoverable from the repository.

All six ProteinGym task configs set awards_medals: false, yet Table 4 prints non-zero Any Medal values for protein engineering; the grader computes medal thresholds from leaderboard size regardless of that flag (biomlbench/grade_helpers.py).

evidence_concerns.message: Supplementary Table 2 runtimes differ from the article's Results for what appear to be the same HG003 comparisons. ONT at 30x and 50x: Clair3 GPU 17 and 20 minutes in the table, 16 and 15 in Results 3.1.1; DeepVariant GPU 48 and 82 in the table, 106 to 128 in the text. PacBio Revio at 30x and 50x: Clair3 GPU 12 and 12 in the table, 23 and 21 in Results 3.1.2; DeepVariant GPU 40 and 53 in the table, 93 and 118 in the text. The table's Clair3 PacBio runtimes equal the macOS M3 Ultra runtime in Results 3.1.3, not the Linux RTX 4090 runtimes. The table and the Supplementary Notes commands give DeepVariant v1.10-beta; Results 3.1 say v1.8. Supplementary Table 3 DeepVariant ONT SNP precision, recall and F1 at 10x and 20x (97.58%, 92.35%, 94.89% and 99.32%, 99.02%, 99.17%) differ from Results 3.2 (97.34%, 92.17%, 94.68% and 98.75%, 98.79%, 98.79%), while the Clair3 values agree. Results 3.2 cite Supplementary Table 2 for the HG001 to HG007 comparison, which is Supplementary Table 4. The hardware, DeepVariant version and runs behind Supplementary Tables 2 and 3 are therefore uncertain. Supplementary Table 1 agrees with Results 3.1.4 except WhatsHap ONT 30x (723 seconds in the table, 724 in the text). Table values are recorded; text values are not.
evidence_concerns.source_locator: Supplementary Tables 1 to 3 (pages 2 and 3) versus article Results 3.1.1 to 3.1.4 and 3.2

All 81 results were then re-read by review/recheck_tables.py, written for this pass and using neither extract/parse_tables.py nor extract/check_tables.py: it takes each table's column spans from the character offsets of that table's own printed header line, assigns every numeric token on a body line to the column whose header centre is nearest, and matches cells to records through each result's source_locator text rather than its ID, checking printed_value, numeric_value, the printed spread and the system the result's evaluation names. Two negative controls confirmed it fails on a swapped pair of values and on a cell shifted into the neighbouring column. A manual check of 16 cells covered column assignment in all three tables, including Table 2's unlabelled PerturbPFN score line, Table 1's third label and value pair on each of its three rows, and Table 3's middle columns. The printed overall score was re-derived as the equal-weight mean of each row's three normalised columns. The 54 descriptive records were read against Sections 2 to 5, Appendices A to E and Tables 4 to 8 of the pinned PDF.

evidence_concerns.message: Appendix A.2 describes the random baseline as predicting hit with probability equal to 'the overall proportion of actual hits in the specific benchmark dataset'. With one pooled rate (485 of 1,175 = 41.3%, Table 3) the expected PPV, sensitivity, F1 and FPR are all about 0.41 and specificity and NPV about 0.59. Table 8 prints PPV 0.47, sensitivity 0.46, F1 0.47, FPR 0.36, specificity 0.64 and NPV 0.63. With each screen's own hit rate (Table 3) the expected values are 0.47, 0.47, 0.47, 0.37, 0.63 and 0.63, which match. One draw at the pooled rate would need sensitivity about 2 standard errors above and FPR about 3 below expectation at once. The baseline therefore probably uses per-screen hit rates, which is information a screen designer would not have before the screen. The expected values were computed by the reviewer from Table 3 counts and are not stored as results. Treat the random row as a per-screen-prevalence classifier, not a matched random-selection comparator.
evidence_concerns.source_locator: Appendix A.2; Table 3; Table 1, row "Random Baseline"; Table 8, row "Random N/A N/A"

evidence_concerns.message: gnomAD presence is only partly fixed. Diagnostics keep their full gnomAD frequency and most are absent from gnomAD (148 of the 200, 386 of the 500), while background variants rarely are. The study's split check flags the gain of Rule + AVI over the rule-based ranking on the 200 SNV cases as possibly due to gnomAD presence in the all1kg check (results/snv_all1kg.json). In the main analysis the same gain is 0.0608 (0.0195 to 0.1149) in cases whose diagnostic is absent from gnomAD and 0.0 in cases where it is found; the difference, 0.0608 (-0.0063 to 0.1377), is not flagged. The split check tests two gains per SNV analysis, both from adding AVI (to the rule-based ranking and to the combined lookups), and none on the indel cases. The other tested gain is not flagged on the 200 or the 500. No other score was tested, so for GPN-MSA, GPN-Star, Evo 2, the single lookups and the combined models the limit is untested, not cleared. It is recorded in each protocol's limitations.

attributes.version: bioRxiv preprint version 1, posted 2026-10-09; full-text PDF (11 pages)
limitations: Preprint, not peer reviewed; single author (712 North Inc.), no funding; none of the evaluated models was developed by the author.
The bioRxiv JATS XML holds metadata only, so the tables were read from the PDF text layer.
Supplementary Tables I to VI and the Zenodo material (doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23105803) were not retrieved.
Table IV prints 15 (13.9%) for AlphaGenome splice scorer and 31 (28.7%) for Genos 10B ClinVar type I errors; 15/107 is 14.0% and 31/107 is 29.0%.
Not archived in the batch: CC BY-NC-ND licence; hash and locators only.

Four printed accuracies differ from those computed from the same row's counts: Table III Borzoi (128-bp) 89.1% (counts give 89.8%); Table IV AlphaGenome (either module) 71.6% (70.5%), Borzoi (128-bp) 80.9% (81.4%) and Genos 10B 61.7% (61.2%).
attributes.hash_scope: SHA-256 of one retrieval of the bioRxiv PDF. bioRxiv stamps the PDF when serving it (ModDate and the second document ID), so later retrievals differ. A reviewer retrieval on 2026-10-12 of the same length (1,823,372 bytes) had SHA-256 e22491e217c7c158528668b38bcb8b9855b89617b807c60b740795a204c84b0a and ModDate D:20261011221204-07'00'. All 168 Table III and IV cells in that copy match the stored results.
attributes.retrieval_note: bioRxiv returned HTTP 429 (rate limit) on earlier attempts the same evening; the PDF request succeeded on its first try.

evidence_concerns.message: The AlphaGenome rows of Tables III, IV and the extended OPA1 positive calls come from scripts that pass a 0-based position to AlphaGenome's 1-based genome.Variant, so each variant was applied one base from its true position. The author labelled the report a bug on 2026-10-20 and said rerunning with the 1-based position substantially improved accuracy. The AlphaGenome results are disputed until the rerun is published; the other models' rows are not affected.
evidence_concerns.source_locator: Table III and Table IV, rows 'ALPHAGENOME (SPLICE SCORER)', 'ALPHAGENOME (JUNCTION SCORER)' and 'ALPHAGENOME (EITHER MODULE)'; scripts 2c8_alphagenome_splicescorer.py lines 98 and 120 and 2c8_alphagenome_junctionscorer.py lines 89 and 110 at commit 3c0c6cc; https://github.com/marcel-2c8/Probing-genomic-foundation-models-2026/issues/2

name: Alavi 2026 supplementary materials (Zenodo 23105803): per-variant model classifications
description: The supplementary archive of Alavi 2026, holding Supplemental Tables IV to VI as workbooks. Table VI lists the 183 multi-gene test-set variants with their HGVS coordinates, which the preprint text does not. Retrieved for the dispute review of the AlphaGenome rows.

attributes.artifact_format: ZIP archive of three Office Open XML workbooks
limitations: Author-deposited supplementary data, not peer reviewed and not a publication in its own right.

Per-variant model calls only: the archive holds classifications ('pathogenic' or 'n.s.'), not the model scores or the thresholds, so the printed sensitivities and specificities cannot be recomputed from it.
The AlphaGenome columns were produced by the scripts carrying the 1-base coordinate offset reported in upstream issue #2, so those calls share the defect of the printed AlphaGenome results.
CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 forbids redistributing the workbooks, so they are not stored in this repository; the archive SHA-256 and classify-table-vi.py are the record.

review.reviewer_note: Recorded by a Claude agent for the 2026-10-23 dispute review (issue #174); no human review claimed. Extractor and reviewer were the same agent.
review.method_note: Every row of Supplemental Table VI was read from the workbook XML and classified by its HGVS coding offset with data/omics/alavi-alphagenome-dispute-20261023/classify-table-vi.py; the counts are that script's output in composition.tsv.
review.note: The preprint text was not changed by the author at the time of review; this records what its own supplement lists.

limitations: Table S9 values are spreadsheet formulas over the TP, FN, TN and FP cells of the same row; the stored results are recorded.
Tables S3 to S5 list 22 true-negative rows (6 muscle, 3 fibroblast, 13 cycloheximide-treated fibroblast); Results and Table S9 use 21 true-negative samples.
Results ('True negative analysis reveals high false positive rates') give an OUTRIDER + GTEx false-positive rate of 83%; Table S9 row 8 (TN 1, FP 4) implies 4 of 5 (80%).
Table S9 gives LeafcutterMD 67 positives (TP 0 + FN 67) while FRASER, run on the same three tissue sets, has 68 (TP 21 + FN 47).
Cell I6 (LeafcutterMD F1) holds a typed 0 rather than the row formula; with precision and recall both 0 the F1 formula would be undefined.

Table S7 true-negative rows do not reproduce Table S9 rows 7 and 8: read as in Tables S3, S4 and S8 ('YES' = no outlier), Table S7 gives OUTRIDER 8 of 9 negative samples without outliers (Table S9: 4) and OUTRIDER + GTEx 1 of 6 (Table S9: 1 of 5). The prose rates (56% and 83%) match Table S9 for OUTRIDER and Table S7 for OUTRIDER + GTEx.

description: Version 2 of the Alavi 2026 preprint, posted with rerun AlphaGenome results after the 1-base coordinate offset in its scripts was fixed.

attributes.version: bioRxiv preprint version 2, posted 2026-10-31; full-text PDF (12 pages)
limitations: Preprint, not peer reviewed; single author (712 North Inc.), no funding; none of the evaluated models was developed by the author.
The bioRxiv JATS XML of version 2 holds metadata only, so the tables were read from the PDF text layer.
Not archived in the batch: CC BY-NC-ND licence; hash and locators only.

Only the AlphaGenome rows of Tables III and IV changed from version 1. Every other cell is printed as in version 1, so the version 1 results stand and the count and percentage mismatches recorded on the version 1 source persist.
Version 2 drops version 1's 'either module' AlphaGenome row, so the version 1 either-module results have no successor.

Methods A still describes the 76 multi-gene positives as substitutions within canonical splice sites of 65 genes; Supplemental Table VI of the version 2 supplement lists the same variants as version 1, of which 26 are at canonical ±1,2 positions.

Methods D says variants were pathogenic 'if their composite score was greater than or equal to 2.60 or their splice-site usage score greater than or equal to 0.93'. Tables III and IV print the composite and splice-site usage as separate rows, which are recorded here as two configurations with one threshold each.

description: Primary source retrieved and hashed for the 2026-10-22 de novo binder design extraction (issue #176).

evidence_concerns.message: The paper prints three different round-1 binder rates and two round-2 expression rates. Section 2.4 gives round 1 as '2.5% (5/201)' and round 2 as 'a 95% expression rate (378 of 400 tested)'; Section 4.1 gives expression as improving 'from 73% to 94%'; Section 4.1 gives the binder percentage as rising 'from 3% in the first round to 13%'. All the printed values are recorded with their locators and none is reconciled here.
evidence_concerns.source_locator: Sections 2.4, 4.1 and 4.2

evidence_concerns.message: Section 4.1 says Figure 8 shows 'the total number of validated binders across the 3 binding thresholds' but no section of the paper defines those three thresholds. No hit definition is therefore recorded for the Figure 8 counts, and the binding protocol's success threshold is left unstated with a reason rather than guessed.
evidence_concerns.source_locator: Section 4.1; Figure 8 caption

attributes.hash_scope: SHA-256 of one retrieval of a mutable web page. The hash describes that retrieval, not a stable artifact.
limitations: Preprint, not peer reviewed.
Written by the competition organisers, who ran the assay. The designs are the entrants'.

Design methods are self-declared: Section 4.2 states that entrants were asked 'to write a short summary of their workflow, which we manually curated and categorized into five design choices'. There is no controlled assignment of methods to designs.

Entrants chose how much effort to spend and how many designs to submit, and Adaptyv hand-selected 101 of 201 round-1 and 300 of 400 round-2 designs to increase diversity, so the tested set is not a sample of any method's output.
Figure 8 reports binders 'across the 3 binding thresholds' and the body does not define those thresholds anywhere.
No conventional comparator arm. EGF and cetuximab were positive controls for the assay, not a design method evaluated on a set of candidates.
Per-method and per-category hit rates are printed only in Figures 3, 8 and 9 and the 60 affinities only in Figure 10; the figure values were not read.

description: Primary source retrieved and hashed for the 2026-10-22 de novo binder design extraction (issue #176).

evidence_concerns.message: Supplementary Data 1 has one row per tested design with a Binding column holding 1, 0 or an empty cell. Treating the non-empty cells as the tested set reproduces the prose counts for BBF-14 (11 tested, 6 binding), Bet v1 (7, 2), CD45 (16, 4), Der f7 (10, 4), Der f21 (7, 4), IFNAR2 (9, 3), PD-1 (53, 13), SpCas9 (6, 6) and CLDN1 (7, 6), but not for PD-L1 (13 non-empty rows with 11 binding against 9 tested with 7 binding in the prose), CrSAS-6 (10 non-empty rows against 9 tested) or CbAgo (2 non-empty rows against 12 tested). The row filter is therefore ambiguous and no value is computed from these rows.
evidence_concerns.source_locator: Supplementary Data 1 (41586_2025_9429_MOESM4_ESM.csv), columns Target, DesignName, Binding; Results prose; Fig. 1b caption

evidence_concerns.message: Fig. 1b's caption defines success as binding observed on SPR, but the PD-1 screen was BLI in a bivalent Fc-fusion format and the CLDN1 screen used soluble analogues. The 46.3% average therefore pools targets measured under different endpoints.
evidence_concerns.source_locator: Fig. 1b caption; Results 'Binders targeting cell-surface receptors' and 'Targeting unexplored binding sites'

limitations: Developer-reported: the BindCraft authors built the pipeline, chose the targets and chose which designs to test.

Fig. 1b prints the per-target numerator and denominator inside graphic boxes. Those boxes are not in the JATS text and were not read from the figure image. Where the Results prose states the counts they are recorded from the prose; where it does not (CrSAS-6, CbAgo) no hit count is recorded.

The assay is not uniform across targets. Fig. 1b's caption defines a successful design as one 'where binding was observed on SPR measurement', but PD-1 was screened by BLI in a bivalent Fc-fusion format and the claudin binders were prescreened against soluble analogues rather than the wild-type target.
Denominators are 6 to 53 designs per target and the tested designs are the top-ranked ones by the authors' own in silico filter, so design and selection are coupled.
No conventional comparator was run. The RFdiffusion comparison in Extended Data Fig. 1c is generation time and in silico success rate, and Extended Data Fig. 7 is reprediction of published designs.
No uncertainty is printed for any per-target rate or count.

attributes.hash_scope: The recorded hash is of the supplement PDF itself, extracted from the Europe PMC supplementaryFiles ZIP (ZIP SHA-256 25050dabd9c66fdb955704095023037f1bbabc3a93b7b61f00344c75df8bdb70 on 2026-10-22; the ZIP is rebuilt per request and its hash is not stable).
limitations: The preprint has not been peer reviewed. The direct bioRxiv PDF returns HTTP 403, so the appendix was taken from the Europe PMC supplementary-files deposit of version 1; the version 2 main-text PDF was not retrieved.
Values were read from the pdftotext (poppler 26.08.0) -layout text layer of the pinned PDF, SHA-256 6e19c85a90c118fd5fd045981a7ebfa5559d9b0a2b4c700b2da0c7393a417c17.
Tables 11, 12 and 14 print one value per cell with no uncertainty. Bootstrap standard errors appear only as error bars in Figure 6, which prints no numbers.

The results of FEP+ are intended to show the maximum attainable accuracy of current (commercial) FEP simulations by manually adjusting the protocol (input preparation, perturbation map, force field) to the system at hand after observing the error with respect to the experiment (appendix D.2.2, 'Baselines'), so the FEP+ arm is not a prospective baseline.
The ABFE arm 'may also represent an optimistic estimate of its prospective performance given that the protocol was optimized based this dataset' (appendix D.2.2, 'Baselines').
The OpenFE arm's cited source is a blog post (Horton, 2025), which is not a primary source under this repository's rules and was not retrieved.

The column headers read 'target avg.' while appendix D.2.2 'Evaluation metrics' defines every regression metric as computed per assay and averaged across assays weighted by compound count. Assays and targets are not the same unit, and the source does not reconcile the two labels.
The paper's claim of being more than 1,000 times faster than FEP is not backed by a measured FEP+ cost: the FEP+ time cell in Table 12 is printed as '-'.
Per-assay and per-series values behind the target averages are not printed anywhere in the supplement. Figure 12 shows per-assay scatter plots for the validation set only and prints no numbers.
